{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZhv-4A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDIqTQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 67, "title": "Implement independent manual serial reads for both standard SNES joypad ports", "body": "## Problem

Manual controller support currently models only port 1. In [`machine.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/0f6e89d38055ccfed22ffff998eb31760bfcbff7/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs), `$4016` reads one shift register, `$4017` returns a constant, and writes to `$4016` latch only the first pad. Consequently, guest software cannot manually read a second standard joypad.

The existing [`memory_open_bus_wram_and_joypad_serial`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/0f6e89d38055ccfed22ffff998eb31760bfcbff7/crates/snes-core/tests/regression.rs) test checks one first-pad pattern and its trailing bit. It does not establish independent port clocks, simultaneous latching, second-port read masks, or comprehensive strobe behavior.

This implements the manual serial prerequisite identified by the latest assessment’s recommendation for two-pad controller support. It is one bounded part of that recommendation.

## Expected outcome

Represent two standard joypads and implement manual reads through the existing system-bank register mirrors. Preserve `Machine::set_buttons`, existing first-pad callers, and the documented bits-15-through-4 input format. Add a minimal core interface for supplying the second pad independently; mask unsupported button bits consistently.

Use [Fullsnes, Controllers and Open Bus](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm) and [Anomie’s Register Doc, `$4016/$4017` JOYSER0/JOYSER1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt) as the documentary references for this contract:

- `$4016` write bit 0 controls the latch shared by both ports. While high, reads report each pad’s B state without advancing its serial position. Returning the latch low leaves both button snapshots ready for reading; repeated low writes do not restart them.
- With the latch low, reading `$4016` returns port 1’s current bit and advances that port; reading `$4017` does the same independently for port 2. Reading either port must not advance the other.
- Each standard pad supplies B, Y, Select, Start, Up, Down, Left, Right, A, X, L, R, then four zero bits. Subsequent reads return one. Host button changes after latching do not replace the captured sequence until another latch operation.
- For the supported standard-pad configuration, data-line 2 returns zero. `$4016` retains CPU open-bus bits 7–2; `$4017` retains bits 7–5 and drives bits 4–2 high. Bit 0 carries the selected pad’s serial data.
- Register mirrors share the same controller state. Reads outside system-bank decoding retain cartridge/WRAM behavior.

Record the supporting reference passages before implementation, including latch/read ordering and unused-line values. Resolve any documentary disagreement explicitly and correct the contract and expectations when evidence requires it. Existing emulator behavior is not a hardware specification.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `0f6e89d38055ccfed22ffff998eb31760bfcbff7`; supplied open-Issue list is empty. No controller improvement duplicates the supplied completed history.

A discriminating reproduction needs no second-pad input API: with automatic polling disabled and a released standard pad on port 2, write `$4016=1`, then `$4016=0`, and read `$4017` seventeen times. The first sixteen data bits should be zero and the seventeenth one; the current handler always returns data bit zero.

The repository’s [`Issue #5 record`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/0f6e89d38055ccfed22ffff998eb31760bfcbff7/docs/issue-5-validation.md) cites Fullsnes and records a modeled 4,224-clock automatic-read busy period. [`Issue #23`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/0f6e89d38055ccfed22ffff998eb31760bfcbff7/docs/issue-23-validation.md) explicitly says zero `$421A–$421F` values do not verify additional controller support. Neither record establishes complete automatic polling phases or manual/automatic interference. Original specification text was unavailable in this checkout; this planning inspection used repository evidence only and ran no tests.

Scope is two standard pads’ **manual** protocol with automatic polling disabled. Exclude automatic polling redesign, second-pad automatic results, manual/automatic interference, peripherals, multitaps, disconnected-device electrical behavior, frontend multiplayer controls, and physical pulse-width accuracy. Preserve existing automatic-read regressions without presenting their timing conventions as independently verified hardware.

Remaining controller work includes shared automatic/manual latch and clock activity; automatic JOY1–JOY4 result routing and update visibility; busy/start/completion and enable-edge timing; interference; and additional device/data-line configurations. All 24 inventory categories retain their supplied status: 21 partial, one implemented_unverified, two unimplemented, zero verified. Controllers remain partial after this Issue.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record authoritative sections supporting the implemented manual protocol, read masks, trailing bits, and latch behavior. Identify unresolved physical timing and automatic-polling questions separately.
- [ ] Implement independent serial state for both ports with a shared latch and compatible first-pad input API. Setting one pad must not overwrite the other. Preserve the existing reset policy of releasing controller inputs; do not claim physical warm-reset accuracy.
- [ ] Add original tests in `crates/snes-core/tests/joypad_serial.rs`. Cover each of the twelve buttons on each port, complementary simultaneous patterns such as `$A590/$5A60`, all sixteen serial positions, and repeated trailing-one reads. Include unequal/interleaved read counts to detect accidental shared advancement.
- [ ] Cover repeated high reads, input changes while high, high-to-low capture, input changes while low, repeated low writes, and relatching both ports. Check driven/open-bus masks using multiple prior bus values and system-bank mirrors, with outside-bank controls. Expected sequences must be independent literals or documented derivations, not production-helper output.
- [ ] Add an original MIT CPU guest that disables automatic polling, latches and manually reads both ports through normal CPU execution, and records numeric results in WRAM. Host code supplies only the cartridge and button inputs. Use explicit instruction/frame deadlines and the natural scheduler; do not inject private serial, raster, or result state. Record source/data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Demonstrate at least one behavior failure against the baseline using a test that compiles there, such as the released second-pad trailing-bit reproduction. A missing new API is not sufficient baseline evidence.
- [ ] Preserve existing first-pad, automatic-read, reset, DMA/HDMA exclusion, diagnostic, hires input, and cleared-game regressions. Extend prohibited `$4016/$4017` DMA/HDMA-read controls to prove neither pad advances; retain the documented approximation for excluded-read bytes.
- [ ] Run and record these pre-merge gates, including both cleared-game builds and all mandatory browser checks. Preserve existing replay inputs, assertions, provenance decisions, and expected game results:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test joypad_serial
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib machine::dma_tests
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dma_access
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py \
  --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(
  cd web
  npx playwright install chromium
  npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
)
```

Use the toolchain prerequisites documented in [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#validate). Existing hardware fixtures must remain source-built from the licensed, pinned inputs. Acquire no commercial ROMs or firmware.

- [ ] Document changes, actual validation results, and remaining limitations. Limited test passage must not be described as full controller accuracy or commercial-game compatibility.

## Optional validation

None required beyond the mandatory checks above. Commercial ROM acquisition is excluded.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
